# Azure Signing Transparency client library for .NET

<!-- cspell:ignore cose merkle scitt -->

`Azure.Security.CodeTransparency` is based on a managed service that complies with a [draft SCITT RFC][SCITT_ARCHITECTURE_RFC]. The service stores [COSE signature envelopes][COSE_RFC] in the Merkle tree and issues signed inclusion proofs as [receipts][SCITT_RECEIPT_RFC].

- [OSS server application source code][Service_source_code]

## Getting started

### Install the package

Ensure you have access to the correct NuGet feed.

Install the client library via NuGet:

```dotnetcli
dotnet add package Azure.Security.CodeTransparency
```

To install a preview release, use the `--prerelease` flag:

```dotnetcli
dotnet add package Azure.Security.CodeTransparency --prerelease
```

### Prerequisites

- A running, accessible Signing Transparency service
- Ability to create `COSE_Sign1` envelopes (see [example script][CTS_claim_generator_script])
- Your signer details (CA certificate) must be configured in the running service (see [configuration options][CTS_configuration_doc])
- Obtain a valid bearer token if service authentication requires one (see [example](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/sdk/confidentialledger/Azure.Security.CodeTransparency/samples/Sample3_UseYourCredentials.md))

### Thread safety

We guarantee that all client instance methods are thread-safe and independent of each other ([guideline](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/dotnet_introduction.html#dotnet-service-methods-thread-safety)). This ensures that the recommendation of reusing client instances is always safe, even across threads.

### Authenticate the client

Obtain a valid bearer token if the service requires authentication (see [example](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/sdk/confidentialledger/Azure.Security.CodeTransparency/samples/Sample3_UseYourCredentials.md)).

## Examples

There are two main use cases: submitting a COSE signature envelope and verifying the cryptographic submission receipt, which proves that the signature file was accepted.

Before submitting the COSE file, ensure the service is configured with the appropriate policy.

Use the following code to submit the signature:

```C# Snippet:CodeTransparencySubmission
CodeTransparencyClient client = new(new Uri("https://<< service name >>.confidential-ledger.azure.com"));
FileStream fileStream = File.OpenRead("signature.cose");
BinaryData content = BinaryData.FromStream(fileStream);
NullableResponse<BinaryData> receiptResponse = await client.CreateEntryAsync(content);
```

Then obtain the transparent statement:

```C# Snippet:CodeTransparencyDownloadTransparentStatement
string entryId = CcfReceipt.GetRegistrationTransactionId(receiptResponse.Value.ToArray());
Console.WriteLine($"The entry ID to use to retrieve the receipt and transparent statement is {{{entryId}}}");
Response<BinaryData> transparentStatementResponse = await client.GetEntryStatementAsync(entryId);
byte[] transparentStatementBytes = transparentStatementResponse.Value.ToArray();
```

After obtaining the transparent statement, you can distribute it so others can verify its inclusion in the service. The verifier checks that the receipt was issued for the given signature and that its signature was endorsed by the service. Because users might not know which service instance the statement came from, they can extract that information from the receipt to create the client for verification.

```C# Snippet:CodeTransparencyVerificationUsingFileBytes
try
{
    var verificationOptions = new CodeTransparencyVerificationOptions
    {
        AuthorizedDomains = { "<< service name >>.confidential-ledger.azure.com" },
        AuthorizedReceiptBehavior = AuthorizedReceiptBehavior.RequireAll,
        UnauthorizedReceiptBehavior = UnauthorizedReceiptBehavior.FailIfPresent
    };
    CodeTransparencyClient.VerifyTransparentStatement(transparentStatementBytes, verificationOptions);
    Console.WriteLine("Verification succeeded: The statement was registered in the immutable ledger.");
}
catch (Exception e)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"Verification failed: {e.Message}");
}
```

If verification completes without exception, you can trust the signature and the receipt. You can then safely inspect the files, especially the payload embedded in the COSE signature envelope.

To learn more about other APIs, see the [samples](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/sdk/confidentialledger/Azure.Security.CodeTransparency/samples).

## Troubleshooting

Response values returned from client methods are `Response` objects, which contain information about the HTTP response such as the HTTP `Status` property and a `Headers` collection with more details.

## Next steps

For more extensive documentation, see the API [reference documentation](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk-for-net/). You can also read more about Microsoft Research's open-source [Confidential Consortium Framework][ccf].

## Contributing

This project welcomes contributions and suggestions. Most contributions require you to agree to a Contributor License Agreement (CLA) declaring that you have the right to, and actually do, grant us the rights to use your contribution. For details, visit https://cla.microsoft.com.

When you submit a pull request, a CLA-bot will automatically determine whether you need to provide a CLA and decorate the PR appropriately (e.g., label, comment). Simply follow the instructions provided by the bot. You will only need to do this once across all repos using our CLA.

proposals.subtype: Expose receipt-profile names and numeric labels as public properties
proposals.explanation: CcfReceipt publishes fifteen fixed-value properties covering the tree algorithm, receipt/header names, COSE/CWT labels and proof-map labels. These are a public protocol-constant surface, not evidence that every label participates in the captured verification path.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The complete static class is in non-generated src, classified as handwritten by the supplied .NET guideline; these declarations expose public API rather than private support constants.

proposals.subtype: Extract a transaction identifier from the first inclusion-proof leaf
proposals.explanation: GetRegistrationTransactionId decodes COSE, reads the unprotected proof map and first inclusion proof, obtains its leaf and returns the second colon-separated internal-evidence field. It returns null for specified missing/empty cases and catches exceptions only around DecodeSign1; later CBOR/leaf errors can propagate. It does not verify the receipt signature.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The non-generated src class implements this concrete nested binary traversal and internal-evidence convention, not a generated protocol operation.

proposals.subtype: Preserve CBOR map values as encoded byte arrays
proposals.explanation: ReadCborMap reads Int32 keys and copies each complete encoded value into a dictionary, then consumes the map end. Assignment replaces earlier entries for repeated keys; the values are not decoded into a typed model here.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The complete non-generated src helper directly implements the CBOR reader loop used by the receipt code.

proposals.subtype: Decode a positional proof-leaf array into a helper model
proposals.explanation: GetLeaf reads a CBOR array's byte string, text string and byte string into InternalTransactionHash, InternalEvidence and DataHash, then consumes the array end. The method does not explicitly check the hash/evidence lengths stated in its comments.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The non-generated src helper explicitly constructs the internal Leaf from positional CBOR reads.

proposals.subtype: Decode nested proof-path arrays into direction/hash elements
proposals.explanation: GetProofElements iterates an outer CBOR array and its nested arrays, repeatedly reading boolean/byte-string pairs into a list of ProofElement objects. It supplies no explicit 32-byte hash check or explicit one-pair-per-inner-array check.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: This complete non-generated src method contains the custom nested reader loop and model construction.

proposals.subtype: Concatenate two or three byte arrays for binary processing
proposals.explanation: The two CombineByteArrays overloads allocate a result sized to the summed input lengths and copy the inputs in order with Buffer.BlockCopy. They do not hash, sign or encode the combined bytes themselves.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The non-generated src class implements these executable binary helpers rather than only declaring constants or model fields.

proposals.subtype: Adapt individual keys or a key set to receipt verification
proposals.explanation: The Verify overloads accept a verification-key object, wrap a key ID and ECDsa, or extract a receipt key ID and look it up in a supplied key set before calling VerifyCore. Explicit null checks cover the object/key-set overloads and a failed lookup throws; key-wrapper validation, ownership and key-set comparison rules are not supplied.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The complete verifier in non-generated src implements these crypto-domain overloads and their dispatch logic.

proposals.subtype: Read a receipt's protected key identifier as UTF-8
proposals.explanation: ExtractReceiptKeyId decodes a COSE Sign1 message, requires its protected KeyIdentifier header and decodes that header's byte value with Encoding.UTF8.GetString. This method alone does not authenticate the header or establish key trust.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The complete non-generated src verifier implements the protected-header extraction explicitly.

proposals.subtype: Validate receipt headers, Merkle inclusion paths and statement digest
proposals.explanation: VerifyCore checks the algorithm, key ID, tree label and required proof structures, and rejects an empty proof array. For each proof it derives a SHA-256 leaf/root accumulator with left/right sibling ordering, passes the root to VerifyDetached with a disposable ECDsa from the supplied key, and compares the leaf data hash with SHA-256 of the signed statement. Failures throw; this source reading is not a cryptographic correctness audit.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The complete non-generated src verifier contains the receipt-profile validation and hashing algorithm rather than merely calling a generated REST method.

proposals.subtype: Look up text values in CBOR maps with string or integer keys
proposals.explanation: The two GetStringValueFromCborMapByKey overloads skip unsupported key/value entries and stop at the first matching key, returning an empty string for guarded empty input, a missing key or a non-text matched value. String keys compare ordinally and integer keys use ReadInt32. Contrary to the broad defensive comment, there is no catch for invalid CBOR or an unexpected root shape, and the remainder after a match is not consumed.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The complete non-generated src helper directly implements both CBOR traversal loops.

proposals.subtype: Construct an identity-service client with pipeline and cache settings
proposals.explanation: CodeTransparencyCertificateClient's constructors default or require options, validate endpoint/options, create diagnostics and a pipeline with empty explicit policy arrays, store the endpoint and initialize a concurrent result dictionary and TTL from options. The empty protected mocking constructor is not separately counted.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The non-generated src partial client contains complete constructor implementations and its own pipeline/cache fields.

proposals.subtype: Cache typed identity responses with a strict age threshold
proposals.explanation: The sync/async identity methods reuse a result when UtcNow minus CreatedOn is less than the configured TTL, returning a typed response with no raw response. On a miss they call the instrumented protocol overload, deserialize the result, cache it only when the raw response is not an error and return both values. Expired entries are not removed by getFromCache; protocol exceptions mark the diagnostic scope failed and rethrow.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The complete non-generated src client explicitly implements the cache lookup/update and both typed/protocol overload families; no generated counterpart is assumed.

proposals.subtype: Build the ledger-identity GET request directly
proposals.explanation: CreateGetLedgerIdentityRequest creates a pipeline message, selects GET, resets the URI to the certificate endpoint, appends /ledgerIdentity/ and an escaped ledger ID, and sets Accept to application/json. This builder contains no request body or explicit API-version query parameter.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The non-generated src client explicitly assembles the HTTP message instead of relying on an unseen generated request builder.

proposals.subtype: Reuse a default request context for uncancelable calls
proposals.explanation: FromCancellationToken returns a shared static RequestContext when the token cannot be canceled; otherwise it allocates a context carrying that token. The method does not clone the shared context or establish an independent concurrency guarantee.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The complete non-generated src client implements the context-selection branch and shared context field.

proposals.subtype: Suppress generated CBOR-request and key-query members
proposals.explanation: Five CodeGenSuppress declarations target CreateGetTransparencyConfigCborRequest and the sync/async GetScittKeys/GetScittKey protocol signatures. The declarations are direct customization intent; this excerpt does not show the resulting generated API or replacement implementations.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The non-generated src partial client carries explicit TypeSpec generator customization attributes rather than relying on absence of a generated header.

proposals.subtype: Compose optional credential authentication with redirect and TLS settings
proposals.explanation: The constructor defaults options, applies retry defaults, derives a service name from the first host label and supplies a certificate client to the TLS transport helper. It builds a pipeline with a per-call redirect policy and either no explicit per-retry policy or AzureKeyCredentialPolicy, then stores endpoint/version. The credential header/prefix values, options factory and redirect-policy body are not captured.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The src partial client outside Generated explicitly builds these policy/transport components and supplies convenience constructor overloads.

proposals.subtype: Replace framework-matching retry count and delay values
proposals.explanation: ApplyRetryDefaults changes MaxRetries from 3 to 10 and Delay from 800 ms to 200 ms when each current value matches its comparison default. It mutates the supplied options and cannot distinguish an explicitly supplied default-valued setting from an unset one; it leaves other values and retry mode unchanged.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The non-generated src helper contains explicit comparisons/assignments and is called by the captured constructor.

proposals.subtype: Extract embedded receipt bytes and attach issuer identifiers
proposals.explanation: GetReceiptsFromTransparentStatementStatic requires the embedded-receipts unprotected header, reads its CBOR byte-string array and pairs each receipt with an extracted issuer. An InvalidOperationException from issuer extraction is replaced with an indexed unknown-issuer label; other exception types and outer decoding failures are not caught here.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The non-generated src client implements the binary traversal, issuer-helper call and explicit fallback-label convention.

proposals.subtype: Read a required issuer string from protected CWT claims
proposals.explanation: GetReceiptIssuerHostStatic requires the protected CWT claims map, reads the issuer-label text with the supplied CBOR helper and throws if it is empty. Despite its name, this body returns the text without URI parsing, hostname normalization or signature verification.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The non-generated src client explicitly implements the header/claim lookup and required-value checks.

proposals.subtype: Install a certificate-validation callback with a deferred clock
proposals.explanation: CreateTlsCertAndTrustVerifier validates its supplied service/client/time-provider arguments and returns transport options whose callback passes the presented certificate and provider to ValidateServerCertificate. The simpler overload supplies a DateTime.Now lambda; time evaluation occurs in the validator rather than being fixed at callback construction.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The non-generated src client explicitly constructs HttpPipelineTransportOptions and assigns its certificate callback.

proposals.subtype: Validate a certificate chain against an identity-service certificate
proposals.explanation: ValidateServerCertificate retrieves an identity certificate, disposes that result and a newly constructed chain, disables revocation checks, allows an unknown authority and adds the identity certificate to ExtraStore. It evaluates the supplied clock per call, requires Build to succeed and compares the resulting root thumbprint with the identity certificate ordinally ignoring case. The identity/parser implementation and full TLS security properties are not established by this body.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The non-generated src client contains the explicit identity-root trust procedure, chain policy assignments and acceptance predicate.

proposals.subtype: Extract an entry identifier from a Location header
proposals.explanation: The helpers take the suffix after the last case-insensitive /entries/ occurrence, or the whole Location value when that segment is absent, remove a query suffix and trim slashes. The public helper throws RequestFailedException if no nonempty identifier remains. This is string processing, not URI validation or demonstrated LRO integration.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The non-generated src client implements both the public response adapter and its concrete header-string parser.

proposals.subtype: Strip unprotected statement headers before receipt verification
proposals.explanation: RunTransparentStatementVerification decodes the signed statement, clears its unprotected headers, obtains a verification key through an uncaptured resolver and passes the re-encoded statement and receipt to CcfReceiptVerifier.Verify. The supplied method does not independently show the resolver's endpoint/issuer checks or network/trust-store policy.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The non-generated src client explicitly composes COSE normalization, key resolution and the captured custom receipt verifier.

proposals.subtype: Prepare receipt verification and normalize an authorized-domain set
proposals.explanation: The captured prefix of VerifyTransparentStatement defaults verification options, extracts receipts and rejects an empty list. It filters blank/raw unknown-prefix entries, trims and deduplicates authorized-domain strings case-insensitively, and rejects an empty normalized set combined with IgnoreAll. The excerpt stops inside a later unauthorized-receipt comparison, so final authorization enforcement, aggregate failures and actual verification dispatch cannot be concluded.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The non-generated src client contains executable policy preparation and guards, even though the rest of this method is outside the bounded capture.
